definition: connection as a debt I carry rather than a tank I refill

settled:
It builds at about an hour a day even with nobody, and a good hour pays it down.

A bad hour puts about ten back on, so avoiding one is worth seeking ten.

The unit is a quality-weighted hour, not a clock hour, and the two differ by an order of magnitude.

About ten thousand hours of it stand behind me, out of twenty years of decline.

Loneliness is the gauge, and watching it moves the needle.

It tracks a need the way my resource bars track theirs, but its shape is different. It is a stock of debt I can pay off, the way sleep debt is, rather than a buffer I draw down, and it neither compounds nor charges interest.

Paying it down costs health, mana, stamina and safety at once, and pauses my recovery while it runs. So my nervous-system capacity is what sets how much of it I can afford.

title: How Far Behind I Am On People
